reference.title: Lying Toe Tap
reference.listing: Page could not be read here (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the toes lower and tap; inhale as the leg returns to tabletop.

prescription.tempo: 1.2 s down, light tap, 1.2 s up
prescription.progression: Both legs at once, then a straighter knee, then dead bugs

cues.text: Lie on your back, arms by your sides. Bring both legs to tabletop: hips and knees at 90 degrees.
Keeping the knee bent, lower the right foot until the toes lightly tap the mat.
Bring the leg back to tabletop without letting the low back lift.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the leg lowers
mistakes.fix: Tap only as low as the back stays flat.

mistakes.mistake: Opening the knee to reach the floor
mistakes.fix: Keep the knee at about 90 degrees; the hip does the moving.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the foot onto the mat
mistakes.fix: A light tap; control the way down.

kinematics.norm: Hips and knees about 90 degrees (standard dead bug and toe tap set-up)
Hip extends from about 90 degrees until the toes touch the mat, knee unchanged (clinical opinion)
Still; the low back stays down (Drysdale 2004)
Slow, about 3 s per tap (clinical opinion)

Escamilla et al. 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
If the low back arches off the mat, the legs are too low for your strength: raise them or bend the knees.
modify: Hands under the buttocks help keep the pelvis tilted and the low back down.
Bend the knees a little to shorten the lever.
Pregnancy, postpartum or diastasis recti: get cleared first, and avoid long supine work later in pregnancy.
regressions: Smaller range: lower the foot only halfway.
Start with one foot resting on the floor.

muscleNotes.core: Transversus and rectus abdominis keep the low back flat while one bent leg lowers and the other hangs in tabletop; lowering a leg pulls the pelvis toward an arch (Drysdale 2004; Escamilla 2016 lists supine leg-lowering among the supine core drills).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris hold the legs up against gravity (clinical opinion; hip flexor EMG rises with leg-lowering work, Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris hold the legs up against gravity (clinical opinion; hip flexor EMG rises with leg-lowering work, Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: The obliques help keep the pelvis level and the ribs down as the legs move off the midline (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: The obliques help keep the pelvis level and the ribs down as the legs move off the midline (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the knee angle steady at about 90 degrees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the knee angle steady at about 90 degrees (clinical opinion).
